actions.name: Gain initial access via compromised credentials and enrolling new device in Duo MFA
actions.description: Russian state-sponsored cyber actors gained initial access to the victim organization via compromised credentials and enrolling a new device in the organization’s Duo MFA.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Obtain credentials via brute-force password guessing attack
actions.description: The actors gained the credentials via brute-force password guessing attack, allowing access to a victim account with a simple, predictable password.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires Windows VM; Windows release and validated image are missing. Supply the release and lawful image reference; no version is assumed.

actions.name: Enroll new device for dormant account due to default Duo MFA configuration
actions.description: The victim account had been un-enrolled from Duo due to inactivity but was not disabled in Active Directory. Duo’s default configuration allowed re-enrollment of a new device for dormant accounts, enabling actors to enroll a new device and obtain access.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Exploit PrintNightmare vulnerability for privilege escalation
actions.description: Russian state-sponsored cyber actors performed privilege escalation via exploitation of the PrintNightmare vulnerability (CVE-2021-34527) to obtain administrator privileges.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated Windows AD DC/member VM fixture and native health checks; this deployment environment has no VM backend/image configured.

actions.name: Modify domain controller hosts file to redirect Duo MFA calls to localhost
actions.description: Actors modified the domain controller file c:\windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts to redirect Duo MFA calls to localhost, preventing MFA server validation and effectively disabling MFA.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Authenticate to victim VPN and make RDP connections to Windows domain controllers without MFA
actions.description: After disabling MFA, actors authenticated to the victim’s VPN as non-administrator users and made RDP connections to Windows domain controllers.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Run commands to obtain credentials for additional domain accounts and bypass MFA for them
actions.description: Actors ran commands to obtain credentials for additional domain accounts and changed the MFA configuration file to bypass MFA for these accounts.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Move laterally to victim’s cloud storage and email accounts and access content
actions.description: Using compromised accounts without MFA enforced, actors moved laterally to the victim’s cloud storage and email accounts and accessed desired content.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The target host has no deployable service, so it is left out of deployment; this step is not reproduced until a service or substitute is supplied for that host.

a6 authentication to VPN and RDP connections occurs after disabling MFA in a5
